contagion_stress_scenario.text:
`historical_scenario_replay` asks what your current portfolio would have lost or gained if each past day's factor moves happened again. You give it `exposures` (currency P&L per unit move of each risk factor) and `historical_factor_returns` (a matrix of past factor moves). It applies each day's moves to those exposures, returns the P&L path and flags the single worst day.

`contagion_stress_scenario` asks a different question: if one shock hits, how far does it spread through a network of connected nodes? You give it an `initial_shock`, a `contagion_matrix` of spillover coefficients, and optionally the number of `rounds`. It adds up the shock plus its repeated spillovers.

In short, the first replays real history against your holdings, while the second propagates a shock through a network you define.

explain.text: `historical_scenario_replay` (Historical Scenario Replay) takes your current portfolio's sensitivities and runs each past day's factor moves through them. You supply `exposures`, the currency P&L per unit move of each risk factor, and `historical_factor_returns`, a matrix of historical factor moves with one row per day and one column per factor. For each day it sums the factor moves times the exposures to give a P&L figure, building a full P&L path. It then identifies the single worst day in that path, so you can see how today's book would have fared under past market conditions.

when.text:
Use Historical Scenario Replay (`historical_scenario_replay`) when you want to see how today's portfolio would have fared through past market moves:

- You want to apply each historical day's factor moves to your current exposures and look at the whole P&L path, not just one figure.
- You need to know which single day in the history would have hurt the current portfolio most.
- You can express your portfolio as currency P&L per unit move of each risk factor (`exposures`) and have a matrix of past factor moves (`historical_factor_returns`).
- You prefer scenarios drawn from what actually happened rather than ones you invent.

If you instead want P&L under a single hypothetical multi-factor shock, `hypothetical_multi_factor_scenario` is listed for that.
